item.research_question: How can a high-entropy alloy simultaneously achieve gigapascal-level superelastic stress, large elastic recovery strain, and a nearly temperature-independent elastic modulus (Elinvar effect) over a wide temperature range?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting under protective argon atmosphere using high-purity raw materials, followed by annealing at 1273 K for 3 h and water quenching; some samples subjected to isothermal aging at 723 K for 1.5 h or exposure to 373 K for 10 days.
item.test_conditions: Compressive superelastic testing from 173 K to 373 K at stress levels up to 1.6 GPa; tensile testing at 323 K down to 173 K; cyclic fatigue testing up to 8 × 10^3 cycles at 1.6 GPa; corrosion testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl and H2SO4 (pH = 3) solutions.
key_findings: At 373 K, the alloy exhibits an elastic strain limit (εE) of 3% and an ultrahigh superelastic stress (σC) of 1.72 GPa.
At room temperature (298 K), the alloy shows a σC of 1.46 GPa, εE of 2.5%, and superelastic recovery strain (εSE) of 1.2%.
At 223 K, the alloy maintains a high σC of 1.26 GPa, significantly higher than the ~0.25 GPa of Ti-50Ni alloy at the same temperature.
The alloy retains a σC over 1 GPa at 173 K, demonstrating a wide temperature range for high superelastic stress.
The average temperature coefficient of modulus is 6.14 × 10^-5 K^-1 from 198 K to 273 K, satisfying the Elinvar effect criterion.
The alloy exhibits a fatigue life of over 8 × 10^3 cycles at a high stress amplitude of 1.6 GPa.
In 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution, the corrosion current density (icorr) is 0.097 μA cm^-2, much lower than the 0.559 μA cm^-2 of Ti-50Ni alloy.
Micropillar compression of the 'Matrix + Cu-rich' phase achieved an ultrahigh σC of 3.2 GPa.
item.mechanism: The multi-functionalities stem from a natural composite microstructure where a highly-distorted B2 matrix phase undergoes a strain glass transition (short-range strain ordering) rather than a long-range martensitic transformation. This matrix is interspersed with non-transforming heterogeneities (β-Nb phase, Cu-rich intermetallics, and Hf-rich oxides). The interactions between the matrix and heterogeneities create high energy barriers for stress-induced martensitic transformation, leading to high σC. The continuous lattice softening of the transformative matrix compensates for the elastic modulus hardening of the non-transforming heterogeneities, resulting in a nearly temperature-independent modulus.
item.limitations: The alloy exhibits stress hysteresis that increases with cooling, which can lead to low efficiency and fatigue damage; the β-Nb phase cannot provide a prominent strengthening effect at room temperature as it undergoes severe plastic deformation before the matrix reaches its critical stress.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that manipulating multiple compositional and structural components in high-entropy alloys is appealing for developing high-performance functional materials and that the high-configuration-entropy strategy is feasible for achieving high performance in physically-parallel ferroelastic systems.
quotes: This alloy also shows good cyclic stability, thermally-stable capacity for elastic energy storage, high micro-hardness and good corrosion resistance, allowing it to operate stably in hostile environments.
Our findings may provide insight into designing high-entropy alloys with unconventional and technologically-important functional properties.

The interactions between the matrix and various heterogeneities give rise to ultrahigh-σC superelasticity with weak temperature dependence; the continuous lattice softening effect of the transformative matrix also compensates for the ever-present elastic hardening of non-transforming heterogeneities, thus yielding nearly temperature independent elastic modulus.
